title: RETRACE: A Modular Framework for Event‐Based Discharge and Suspended Sediment Analysis
content:
Abstract

High-resolution measurements of river discharge and suspended sediment allow for the analysis of sediment transport in unprecedented detail. However, disentangling the interplay between upstream sediment supply and local hydraulic controls still poses a challenge, as traditional methods rely on a-priori knowledge of sediment sources, sinks, and their connectivity. In this study, we introduce Routing and Event Time-differencing for Response Analysis of mass Changing Events (RETRACE), a time series analysis framework that leverages coupled measurements of discharge and suspended sediment concentration between two stations. The framework is organized into five modules that semi-automatically extract sediment transporting events and classify them objectively into those controlled by catchment supply or channel hydraulics. Each event is described by its flow properties and changes in suspended sediment load during the event. Events are then classified using a linear regression model, grouping them by the variable with the highest predictive power in explaining sediment load variability. In an example application to a river reach of the Arc–Isère catchment (French Alps), RETRACE shows that flow unsteadiness and incoming sediment concentration are the dominant variables driving changes in sediment load during events. The framework also shows a clear seasonal shift in the controls: channel processes prevail in spring and autumn (66% and 50% of mass, respectively), while catchment processes drive suspended sediment changes in summer (46% of mass). RETRACE captures how processes acting at different spatio-temporal scales affect suspended sediment transport in river systems, advancing the interpretation of high-resolution monitoring data from multiple stations.
